questions.q: Why must you never open a microwave oven to salvage parts, even after unplugging it?
choices: The magnetron is too heavy to remove safely
Its high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal 4,000+ V even when unplugged
Microwaves contain no useful low-voltage parts
Opening it voids the manufacturer's warranty
questions.explain: A microwave's high-voltage capacitor can store a lethal charge of 4,000 V or more long after the oven is unplugged. The same stored-charge danger applies to CRT TVs (20,000–30,000 V anode) and mains power supplies — recycle all of these whole, never open them.

questions.q: On Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm, a plain system-wide 'pip install something' fails with 'externally-managed-environment'. What does PEP 668 want you to do instead?
choices: Always add --break-system-packages to force the install
Run the command twice with sudo
Use 'sudo apt install python3-<name>', or create and activate a venv then pip install inside it
Switch from python3 back to python2
questions.explain: PEP 668 marks the system Python as externally managed to stop pip breaking the OS. The correct fixes are 'sudo apt install python3-<name>' or a virtual environment (python3 -m venv myenv; source myenv/bin/activate; pip install ...). The --break-system-packages flag is discouraged — its name is the warning.

questions.q: On an LED, how do you identify the cathode (the negative leg)?
choices: It is the longer leg, on the rounded side of the plastic rim
It is the shorter leg, on the flat side of the plastic rim
Both legs are identical; LEDs have no polarity
It is whichever leg is connected through the resistor
questions.explain: The cathode (−) is the shorter leg and sits on the flat edge of the plastic rim; the anode (+) is the longer leg. Current must enter the long leg and leave the short leg or the LED stays dark — though wiring it backwards does no harm at these low voltages.

questions.q: A resistor has the colour bands brown–black–red–gold. What is its value?
questions.explain: Reading digit–digit–multiplier–tolerance: brown (1), black (0), red (×100) gives 10 × 100 = 1,000 Ω = 1 kΩ, and gold means ±5%. (For comparison, a 330 Ω resistor is orange–orange–brown–gold.)

questions.q: You salvage an LED from an old device but its legs were trimmed to the same length. Which multimeter setting confirms which leg is the anode and that the LED still works?
choices: The DC volts setting, probes on each leg
The continuity (beep) setting
The resistance (Ω) setting
The diode-test setting — red probe on the anode makes it glow faintly
questions.explain: The diode-test setting checks direction and health: with the red probe on the anode and black on the cathode, a good LED glows faintly and shows a forward voltage (~1.5–3.5 V). Swapping the probes leaves it dark, which tells you the polarity even when the legs are the same length.
